| `20260813.204200` | [`20260813-204200_reds76-witness-contains-loom.bron`](20260813-204200_reds76-witness-contains-loom.bron) | **REDS #76 — the apostrophe lantern becomes a loom: witnesses check claims with native `contains`** — the apostrophe-in-GREEN-line red fired a fifth time at HUNK49 (the witness assertion went RED while the binary plainly printed GREEN). The HUNK39 · 40 · 42 · 43 logs each booked it and each fixed it the same reflexive way — strip the apostrophe from the print line. Reds-first says a lantern that fires this many times becomes a **loom**, a structural fix rather than a fifth reflex. The root cause: `run ["sh" "-c" "printf '%s' '${out}' | grep …"]` interpolates the selftest output into a shell single-quoted string, so any apostrophe in the output (`cursor's`, `paint's`) closes the quote early and mangles the printf. The fix routes the output through no shell at all — Rishi's native `str contains "needle"` tests a Rishi value, so an apostrophe in the haystack can never break a check.
